newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA BUILD BIG LEAD, STRIKE EARLY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA BUILD BIG LEAD, STRIKE EARLY.

text.p: Australia amassed a daunting lead and then knocked the top off the West Indies second innings by tea on the third day of their fourth test match at the Adelaide Oval on Monday.

The West Indies were lanquishing at 39 for 2 at tea after Australia were finally dismissed half an hour into the session for 517, having added 83 to their overnight score for the loss of five wickets.
Australia's huge first innings lead of 387 and the loss of two early wickets means the West Indies will struggle to survive past the fourth day and make Australia bat again.

Victory for Australia, which now looks increasingly likely, would clinch a series win and ensure the hosts retain the Frank Worrell trophy they won in the Caribbean in 1995, as they lead the series 2-1.
The West Indies began the day well, claiming Australia's remaining five wickets inside the first session and a half for just 83 runs. Australia had been scoring at about 100 a session.
But if the West Indies thought they were fighting their way back into the match, the brittleness of their batting line-up soon dashed those hopes.

Australia's strike fast bowler Glenn McGrath had the West Indies' openers groping and jumping from his first over, when a sharply rising ball ripped into Sherwin Campbell's ribcage and dribbled back on to the base of the stumps.
Campbell held his breath as the bails jiggled and fell back into place and he was not out.
Adrian Griffith (1) was not so lucky, edging a rising brute of a ball from McGrath's second over to Steve Waugh at slip as he tried to protect his throat.

Then the main destroyer in the West Indies first innings, left armed legspinner Michael Bevan, struck, removing the dangerous Shivnarine Chanderpaul for eight with a leg spinner that fizzed off the pitch, caught the edge and was grabbed by a diving Mark Taylor at first slip.
Chasing the 387 to make Australia bat again, the West Indies have not bettered 181 in their last four innings.
